anchors.3: Solves the required problem end to end with implementation evidence.
anchors.5: Anticipates relevant edge cases and demonstrates their handling.

anchors.1: When agentic behavior is explicitly required, only a single prompt with no evidenced agentic control flow is implemented.
anchors.3: Tool-calling and state are implemented and reached.
anchors.5: Purposeful reflection or critique loops improve behavior with bounded failure handling.

anchors.1: When model-based behavior is explicitly required, model choice is unjustified and effective guardrails are absent.
anchors.3: Model fit is justified and meaningful input/output validation is used.
anchors.5: Appropriate routing, caps and fallbacks are implemented and supported by evidence.

anchors.1: A tracked likely live secret or comparably severe evidenced security failure.
anchors.3: Readable, maintainable implementation with usable setup and operating documentation.
anchors.5: Reproducible operation, robust failure handling and no material issues found within the stated review coverage.

anchors.1: No meaningful evaluation or observability is evidenced.
anchors.3: Relevant unit tests and useful diagnostic observations cover the main behavior.
anchors.5: Representative golden evaluations, failure cases and actionable observability demonstrate reliable behavior.

anchors.1: The intended user interface or integration is broken.
anchors.3: A clear, usable primary interface such as a clean CLI completes the main workflow.
anchors.5: Appropriate streaming, human-in-the-loop interaction and robust integration handle the intended user workflow.

anchors.1: Judge evidence shows only a scripted happy path and an inability to explain the implementation.
anchors.3: Judge evidence shows the application running live and surviving one hostile probe.
anchors.5: Judge evidence covers cold start, a model swap and judge-chosen input with credible technical explanations.
